newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks climb, awaiting news on electricals.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks climb, awaiting news on electricals.

text.p: Chilean stocks climbed in morning trade following Wall Street, with the market awaiting news on a ruling from a government anti-monopoly board affecting energy investment company Enersis.
The blue-chip IPSA index rose 0.68 percent to 133.01 points after about an hour of trade. The general IGPA index was up 0.32 to 5723 points.

Prices were helped by heavy rain in Santiago, which eased lingering concerns about the effects of drought on electrical shares, and demand for Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts, brokers said.
The biggest gainers included hydroelectric stocks like Colbun, up 2.2 percent to 46 pesos, and Endesa, up 1.3 percent to 312 pesos.

A year-long drought practically ended with heavy rains last month but water levels at reservoirs are still below normal, electric companies say. Torrential rains in Santiago starting Wednesday night increase the likelihood there will no power rationing this year.

Also in the electrical sector, the market was awaiting a ruling from the anti-monopoly commission on whether Enersis will be able to continue with its "vertical integration" in energy generation, transmission and distribution, brokers said.
A favorable ruling was likely to help prices for Enersis, its generation unit Endesa and distribution unit Chilectra, brokers said. Enersis' transmission company, Transelec, is not publicly traded.

A state anti-monopoly prosecutor has charged that Enersis' involvement in every stage of electricity, from generation to distribution, has had a chilling effect on the development of competition in the national power industry.
The president of the anti-monopoly commision, Raul Zurita, told Reuters on Tuesday that it had reached a unanimous ruling and that it would be announced Wednesday.
